In addition, sodium concentration increased in well 16B and concentrations of all major cations increased at alluvium well 18, Tract II. It appears that most published data are still too incomplete to detect any strong quantitative trends or changes in the water quality of the above wells.
Strontium concentrations from the samples taken in fall 1975 range from 0.42 to 18.79 mg/l (average of 5.5 mg/l), showing a 60 percent increase over those reported in the summer of 1975.
Sulfate concentrations in alluvium wells along East Fork Sarpy
Creek increased significantly downstream from well 20 to 13. On August
11, the upstream well (20) provided a sulfate concentration of 788 mg/l;
wells 12 and 13 produced sulfate concentrations of 1,007 mg/l and 1,492
mg/l, respectively, on July 8 (Dames and Moore, 1975, p. 19). A similar\nincrease was noted in sulfate concentration in the downstream direction
of the surface waters of Sarpy and East Fork Sarpy Creeks.
The Romine well is completed to the lower Sub-Robinson unit in the valley of Spring Creek in Tract II. Cation concentrations decrease in the order magnesium (250 mg/l, sodium (170 mg/l), and calcium (140 mg/l); bicarbonate (1000 mg/l) is greater than sulfate (850 mg/l; the only significant trace metals are strontium (4 mg/l) and boron (1 mg/l).
